Hi Liam — thanks for the clear ask, and happy to take point on the questionnaire with Marissa. Quick answers below; happy to expand in the questionnaire or a 30-min call.

SOC 2:
- Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II (security & availability) with the most recent audit period ending 2025-11-01. We can share a redacted SOC 2 report summary (attached: SOC2-report-summary.pdf) via a secure link or NDA if needed.

GDPR / data residency / deletion:
- Residency: For hosted accounts we offer region pinning to us-east-1 or eu-west-1. For Amaya we can discuss EU-only deployment if required; Dedicated/Private options available for strict residency needs.
- Deletion SLA for customer data: Customer-initiated permanent deletion requests (delete account + data) are completed within 30 calendar days for primary stores. That includes customer PII and application data stored in Redwood-managed stores.
- Data subject requests: We provide an API and support flow to export and remove user data; typical turnaround is within the same 30-day window (scope-dependent).

Logs & backups:
- Application logs (request traces, debug logs): default retention 90 days. Configurable up to 365 days for Enterprise plans.
- Access and audit logs: default 180 days; can be extended to 3 years on request (additional retention add-on).
- Backups / snapshots: incremental backups are retained for 90 days by default; we keep immutable snapshots for up to 180 days to support point-in-time recovery and forensic needs.
- Backups containing customer data are rotated and pruned according to the retention policy; when a permanent deletion is executed we remove the primary data and flag backups for purge within the backup retention window. In practice, full removal from all immutable snapshots can take up to the backup retention window (up to 180 days) unless a paid accelerated purge option is accepted and agreed in contract.

Legal holds & e-discovery:
- We can place a retention hold on a customer's datasets to prevent automated purging; holds require a written request and are subject to commercial terms.

Next steps:
- We'll start answering the vendor questionnaire when you upload it. Marissa will coordinate scheduling.
- If EU-only residency is a firm requirement, please confirm and we'll loop in the Private deployment team for an architecture and pricing proposal.

Attachments: SOC2-report-summary.pdf (redacted) and Data-Retention-SLA-table.xlsx

Best,

Hi Liam — Rishi here (product/security liaison). Adding a couple of implementation notes on retention and deletion SLA mechanics so your architects have concrete expectations.

Technical notes:
- Deletion flow: a customer delete request triggers a workflow that removes records from the primary data store and initiates a background job to scrub indices and caches. Once the workflow completes we return a deletion confirmation.

- Backup purge: as Neha noted, backups are on a retention schedule. For standard accounts the backup retention window sets the upper bound on when data may be fully purged from snapshots. We offer an accelerated purge (contracted) that initiates a manual snapshot purge; typical completion for accelerated purge is 7–30 days depending on dataset size and replication scope.

- Logging scopes: we separate telemetry (metrics) from request-level logs; metrics are aggregated and retained longer without user-identifiable data. Request-level traces contain identifiers and follow the log retention schedule above.

If Amaya would like faster guarantees for backup purges or a custom legal-hold workflow, we can include those terms in the Dedicated/Private offer (contract addendum).

1) Liam — please upload the questionnaire (we'll assign Neha as primary owner).
2) Marissa — let's propose the following slots for a 30-min security walkthrough: Tue 6/16 10:00 PT or Wed 6/17 09:00 PT.
3) If Amaya confirms EU-only requirement, Marissa to loop in Solutions (cc: priyom_das) and we'll scope Private deployment.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing.
